question.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}4x\,dV
$$

where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 1\},
$$

and $D$ is a finite region in $xz$-plane enclosed between the $x$-axis, the $z$-axis, and the curve $z+{x}^{2}=1$ in the first quadrant.
question.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a mixed integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}4x\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}4x\,dy]dA.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}4x\,dy]dA & ={∬}_{D}4x[y]_{y={x}^{2}}^{y=1}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}4x(1-{x}^{2})\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

We must now evaluate this double integral over the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14227375/assets/40624d9441af334e6025fccd70040cd7cf9eca972da4aa69a9f9a0133465a7be.png)

 

We can evaluate our double integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}4x(1-{x}^{2})\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}4x(1-{x}^{2})\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4x(1-{x}^{2})[{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}1\,dz]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4x(1-{x}^{2})[z]_{z=0}^{z=1-{x}^{2}}dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4x(1-{x}^{2})(1-{x}^{2}-0)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4x(1-{x}^{2})^{2}\,dx \\  & =-2{\int }_{0}^{1}(-2x)(1-{x}^{2})^{2}\,dx \\  & =-2{[\frac{(1-{x}^{2})^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-2(0-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
